title: Who Should I Call for Dryer Vent Repair?
h1: Who Do You Call for Dryer Vent Repair?
description: For a clogged, crushed or poorly routed dryer vent, call a dryer vent specialist or an HVAC and duct company. Here is who handles what and when to call.
quick_answer: Call a dryer vent specialist or an HVAC and duct company for problems with the vent itself: clogs, crushed or disconnected ducts, bad routing or a broken exterior cap. Call an appliance repair technician if the dryer machine is the problem, such as a bad heating element, belt or sensor.
body:
When a dryer stops drying well, the first question is whether the problem is the dryer or the vent. They're fixed by different trades, and calling the wrong one wastes a visit. A quick check at home usually points you in the right direction.

Is the problem the dryer or the vent?

A simple check helps sort it out. Pull the dryer a few inches from the wall, disconnect the hose from the back and run it on a heat setting for a few minutes. Feel the air coming out of the dryer.

  • Strong, hot air from the dryer points to a vent problem. The machine is doing its job, but the air can't get out of the house.
  • Weak or cool air from the dryer points to the machine, such as a heating element, gas valve, blower wheel or thermostat.

Don't run the dryer this way for long, and never do this test with a gas dryer, since it releases combustion gases indoors. With a gas dryer, check the outside cap instead.

Who fixes dryer vent problems?

Call a dryer vent specialist or an HVAC company that does duct and vent work for:

  • Lint clogs in the vent line or at the exterior cap
  • Crushed, kinked or disconnected duct behind the dryer or in the wall
  • Vents that run too long or have too many turns
  • Vents that end in the attic, garage or crawl space
  • Broken, stuck or screened exterior caps
  • Roof vents that are hard to reach or keep clogging
  • Birds or rodents nesting in the vent
  • Water collecting in the vent line

These jobs need the right tools: rotary brushes, high-powered vacuums, airflow checks and, for repairs, rigid metal duct and proper fittings. Some vents run through attics, walls and roofs, so access and experience matter.

Who fixes the dryer itself?

An appliance repair technician handles the machine: heating elements, igniters, gas valves, belts, rollers, drum bearings, door switches, moisture sensors and control boards. If your dryer won't heat, won't spin, makes grinding noises or shows error codes, start there.

Keep in mind that a clogged vent can cause some of those failures. Overheating from poor airflow can blow a thermal fuse or wear out a heating element. If the machine keeps needing the same repair, have the vent checked too.

What does a dryer vent visit usually include?

A good visit starts with an airflow check at the exterior cap, then a look at the transition hose and the visible parts of the run. The technician cleans the full line from the dryer to the outside, clears the cap and checks the airflow again. If they find crushed, disconnected or foil duct, they'll show you and explain the repair options before doing anything else.

What about a handyman or roofer?

A handyman can replace a cracked wall cap or swap a flimsy foil hose for a metal one. For anything inside walls or attics, rerouting, or a full cleaning of a long run, a vent specialist is the better choice.

A roofer may be involved if a roof vent cap needs to be replaced and flashed properly to prevent leaks. Many vent technicians can handle the cap as part of the vent work.

When is it urgent?

Stop using the dryer and get the vent checked soon if you notice:

  1. A burning smell while the dryer runs
  2. The dryer or laundry room feels very hot
  3. Clothes are hot to the touch but still damp
  4. No airflow at the outside cap
  5. Lint coming out around the dryer or from the wall

Lint is very flammable, and a blocked vent traps heat. If you ever see smoke or flames, get out and call 911.

What should I ask before hiring someone?

A few good questions:

  • Do you clean the entire vent run, from the dryer to the exterior cap?
  • Will you check airflow before and after?
  • Do you repair or replace damaged sections with rigid metal duct?
  • Can you reroute the vent if it's too long or ends in the wrong place?
  • Do you have a California contractor license?

faqs: Can an appliance repair technician clean my dryer vent?

Some will clean the short hose behind the dryer, but many don't clean the full vent run through walls, attics or roofs. For a complete cleaning or vent repair, a dryer vent specialist or duct company is usually the better call.
How do I know if my dryer vent needs repair, not just cleaning?

If the duct is crushed, disconnected, made of foil or vinyl, sags, or ends somewhere other than outdoors, it needs repair. A technician can inspect the run with a camera or airflow check during a cleaning visit.
Can I repair a dryer vent myself?

You can replace a crushed hose behind the dryer with a short metal transition hose and clean the lint screen. Work inside walls, attics or on the roof, and any rerouting, is best left to a professional.
How long does dryer vent repair take?

A cleaning or simple repair usually takes a single visit. Rerouting a vent or replacing a long run through an attic or wall can take longer depending on access. The technician can give you a clear estimate after looking at your setup.
